profile.campus: Philadelphia metro, Pennsylvania (Flexential's former Allentown/DC7 building; Flexential's only current active Pennsylvania location is Philadelphia - Collegeville, elsewhere in this registry)
profile.reading:
This facility, previously known as Flexential's DC7 site at 744 Roble Road, Allentown, Pennsylvania, has been vacated by Flexential and is now on the market for lease or sale through a third-party listing agent, Five9s Digital, according to independent Lehigh Valley trade press (IDCNOVA) reporting on the commercial listing. The property was originally built out by InetU, founded around 1996 and acquired by ViaWest in 2015; ViaWest merged with Peak 10 in 2017 to form Flexential in 2018. The current listing describes a single-story, 3.4-acre, 46,800-square-foot facility with 2.9 MW of backup generation and 849 kW of UPS capacity as currently installed, expandable toward 40 MW. Flexential's own current data center site, checked directly this session, no longer lists any Allentown or Bethlehem facility; its only current Pennsylvania location is Philadelphia - Collegeville, elsewhere in this registry. This row is documented here as a former Flexential facility rather than deleted, per registry policy, so the site's history and current market status remain traceable. Pennsylvania's data center market overall trails the major East Coast hubs of Northern Virginia and the New York/New Jersey corridor, with the Lehigh Valley representing a smaller submarket than Philadelphia's own suburbs.

Pennsylvania's data center sales-tax exemption, established in 2016 as a refund capped at $5 million and restructured in 2021 into an uncapped exemption with reduced state tracking ability, is now projected by the Shapiro administration to cost $188 million in the 2026-27 fiscal year, rising to $517 million by fiscal year 2031, with total losses since inception potentially reaching about $2 billion by mid-2031, according to Spotlight PA's reporting. Cryptocurrency miners were banned from the program in 2024. State Rep. Greg Vitali introduced a bill to repeal the exemption, but acknowledged uncertain prospects given Governor Shapiro's public support for the program; Shapiro's own budget proposal assumes the exemption continues, with conditional added benefits for developers meeting environmental and employment standards.

reading.body:
This facility is not currently operational. Flexential vacated the Allentown site and placed it on the market for lease or sale in 2026, so it contributes zero capacity to the grid today.

The property itself is modest in scale and substantially built out. The listing describes 46,800 square feet with 2.9 MW of backup generation and 849 kW of UPS currently installed, expandable toward 40 MW. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the current UPS capacity would support roughly 20 racks, while the expansion target of 40 MW would support approximately 1,000 racks. The expansion potential depends on whether the electrical infrastructure to support it was ever installed before the facility was vacated.

Pennsylvania has 14 mapped data centers, of which only 4 publish power figures totaling 22.2 MW. This vacant facility would rank fifth by published capacity if it were operating, but its relevance to AI infrastructure is contingent on whether a new operator acquires it and invests in the stated expansion path. The facility is being marketed by a third party, not the operator who built it out.
